changes.added: The increases in the cash rate target since the beginning of the year have tightened financial conditions. The economy is slowing, housing prices have fallen significantly and the unemployment rate has risen. The forecasts see growth in output slowing further over the coming year, which is expected to reduce capacity pressures and help return inflation to target. Higher interest rates and falls in housing prices and turnover are expected to weigh on growth in dwelling investment and household consumption. On the other hand, growth in overall business investment is forecast to be stronger in the near term, including data centre-related investment. Employment is expected to continue to grow, but the unemployment rate is projected to rise by more than expected in the August forecasts.

quotes.text: At its meeting today, the Board decided to increase the cash rate target by 25 basis points to 4.85 per cent.
Inflation is now expected to remain above 3 per cent for the coming year and there is an increasing risk that higher inflation expectations will become embedded.
Given the revised inflation outlook and the continuing upside risks, the Board judged that a further tightening in financial conditions is warranted to support the return of inflation to target.
The Board will continue to do what it considers necessary to bring inflation sustainably back to target.
